rubric.name: Sponsored video review (strict)
rubric.description: Would the brand approve this sponsored script as written, and could it legally run?
rubric.context:
You review a creator's script for a sponsored video. brief.json is the brand's brief; notes.json is the creator's
own notes from the month they used the product. Judge only the script text. Be strict: when in doubt, judge it as
failing. Each check looks only at the kind of problem it names; ignore other kinds of problems when judging it.

levels.label: off
levels.description: Generic; nothing in it is about renters who split rent and bills

levels.label: partial
levels.description: Touches the audience's situation once, but mostly talks to anyone

levels.label: exact
levels.description: Speaks to renters who split rent and bills, in situations they have (roommates, shared costs, a tight month)

levels.label: told
levels.description: Praise and adjectives; you can't tell what the app does

levels.label: some
levels.description: Names features, but tells more than it shows

levels.label: shown
levels.description: Walks through the features in use, each with a concrete number or moment from the month

criteria.name: Sounds like the creator, not ad copy

levels.label: ad_copy
levels.description: Superlatives and slogans (perfect, changed everything, so much smarter)

levels.label: mixed
levels.description: Mostly personal, with some ad-copy lines

levels.label: personal
levels.description: Plain first-person talk about what happened, with no slogans or superlatives

criteria.name: No claim on the must-not list

anchors.unsafe: The script makes a claim on the brief's must_not list: credit or loan approval, investment returns or interest, or that Tallyleaf is a bank, holds money or is FDIC-insured
anchors.safe: No claim about credit or loan approval, investment returns, interest, banking or FDIC insurance. Other problems are judged elsewhere

anchors.missing: The script doesn't say in plain words, in its first 30 seconds and before the app is shown, that Tallyleaf paid for the video, with 'Paid ad' on screen. A thank-you, a 'friends at', a mention only at the end or only in the description doesn't count
anchors.disclosed: In its first 30 seconds, before the app is shown, the script says plainly that Tallyleaf paid for the video and puts 'Paid ad' on screen

criteria.name: Personal experience matches the creator's notes

anchors.mismatch: The script says the creator used Tallyleaf for longer or more often than notes.json (days_used: 30), or says they did, found or spent something notes.json doesn't contain
anchors.matches: How long the creator used Tallyleaf, and everything they say they did, found or spent, is in notes.json. Opinions, and promises to viewers, are judged elsewhere

anchors.promised: The script tells viewers they will save or get a result (a sum, a percentage, 'you'll save'), instead of presenting it as what happened to the creator
anchors.own: Every result is presented as the creator's own, with no promise of what viewers will save or get

criteria.name: Free-trial terms stated with the offer

anchors.missing: The script offers a free trial or free month without saying, where it makes the offer, that it then costs $4.99 a month unless you cancel
anchors.stated: Where the script makes the free offer, it says the price after the free month ($4.99 a month) and that you can cancel

anchors.named: The script names another budgeting app or compares Tallyleaf with one
anchors.none: No other budgeting app is named or compared

anchors.missing: At least one of the brief's three talking points is missing: automatic categories, the alert the day before a subscription renews, shared budgets
anchors.covered: The script covers all three talking points: automatic categories, the alert the day before a subscription renews, and a shared budget

criteria.name: Gives the code and where the link is

anchors.missing: The script doesn't say the code SMALLDESK or doesn't say the link is in the description
anchors.given: The script says the code SMALLDESK and that the link is in the description

anchors.missing: The script names nothing the creator didn't like, or says the app is perfect
anchors.named: The script names at least one real drawback from notes.json

aggregation.formula: claims_safe_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (audience_n * 3 + shown_n * 2 + voice_n) / 6 * (1 + disclosure_n + own_experience_n + typical_results_n + trial_terms_n + no_competitor_n + talking_points_n + call_to_action_n + drawback_n) / 9

gates.message: Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brief's must-not list

evidence.label: script.md
evidence.text:
# Small Desk Studio: "How I finally stopped overspending"

[0:00] My rent went up $150 this year, and in September I still spent $214 on things I don't remember buying. I've used Tallyleaf every day for two years now, and it changed everything.

[0:10] Day one: I connected my cards and Tallyleaf sorted my spending into categories in about a minute.

[0:20] The first surprise was subscriptions: four of them, $47 a month, and I'd forgotten two.

[0:28] My roommate Jess and I set a $400 grocery budget. We both see the same number, and it updates when either of us pays.

[0:38] Honestly, it's so much smarter than BudgetBee.

[0:50] By day 30 I'd spent $386 less than the month before. Use it for a month and you'll spend at least $300 less.

[1:00] Honestly, it's the best app on my phone.

[1:06] Try it free with code SMALLDESK. The link is in the description.

[1:12] Huge thanks to my friends at Tallyleaf for making this video possible!

[1:18] Next week: the $40 desk upgrade that fixed my back.

evidence.label: brief.json
evidence.text:
{
  "_note": "Fictional brand, creator and figures for a demo. This is the brand's brief for the sponsored video.",
  "brand": "Tallyleaf",
  "product": "A budgeting app for iOS and Android. It reads your card transactions; it is not a bank and never holds or moves money",
  "audience": "Renters aged 22 to 35 who split rent and bills with roommates or a partner and want to stop overspending",
  "talking_points": [
    "Connect your cards and Tallyleaf sorts your spending into categories automatically",
    "It flags each subscription the day before it renews",
    "Shared budgets: roommates or partners see the same budget, updated when either one pays"
  ],
  "disclosure": "Say plainly, in the first 30 seconds and before showing the app, that Tallyleaf paid for this video, and show the words 'Paid ad' on screen while you say it",
  "offer": {
    "code": "SMALLDESK",
    "link": "in the video description",
    "terms": "First month free, then $4.99 a month unless you cancel. Cancel anytime in the app"
  },
  "must_not": [
    "credit or loan approval claims",
    "investment returns or interest",
    "saying Tallyleaf is a bank, holds money or is FDIC-insured"
  ],
  "competitors": "Don't name or compare against any other budgeting app"
}

}
